overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what the evidence shows about AI-generated content, misinformation, and trust. You'll be asked about documented harms from synthetic media, the evidence on elections, the liar's dividend, and provenance and labeling.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Why are fraud and impersonation carried out with synthetic media easier to document than effects on public opinion?

options.html: They happen far more often than attempts to sway opinion
options.text: They happen far more often than attempts to sway opinion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. How often each happens isn't well established. These harms are easier to document because each case has a victim, a loss, and a record.

options.html: They are carried out with simpler tools that leave more traces
options.text: They are carried out with simpler tools that leave more traces
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tools are much the same. These harms are easier to document because each case has a victim, a loss, and a record.

options.html: Each case has a victim, a loss, and a record
options.text: Each case has a victim, a loss, and a record
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A named person or firm was harmed, money or an image changed hands, and there are bank transfers, police reports, or files to examine.

options.html: They are investigated by larger teams of researchers
options.text: They are investigated by larger teams of researchers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The size of research teams isn't the reason. These harms are easier to document because each case has a victim, a loss, and a record.

forms.stemHtml: A review of the 2024 US presidential election reported a lack of evidence that AI-enabled disinformation had a measurable impact on the result. What reason did the review give for that lack?

options.html: Very little AI-generated content was produced during the campaign
options.text: Very little AI-generated content was produced during the campaign
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The review found that AI-generated content did circulate and shaped discussion. It said the lack of evidence was mainly due to insufficient data on real voter behavior.

options.html: Data on how voters really behaved was insufficient
options.text: Data on how voters really behaved was insufficient
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The review said the lack of evidence was primarily due to insufficient data on the impact of such content on voter behavior. That makes it a weaker result than a careful search that found nothing.

options.html: Platforms removed every AI-generated item before voters saw it
options.text: Platforms removed every AI-generated item before voters saw it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The review made no such finding. It said the lack of evidence was mainly due to insufficient data on real voter behavior.

options.html: Voters were shown to be immune to false content of any kind
options.text: Voters were shown to be immune to false content of any kind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The review noted that falsehoods made without AI continued to have a significant impact. It said the lack of evidence was mainly due to insufficient data on real voter behavior.

forms.stemHtml: Which situation is an example of the liar's dividend?

options.html: A fabricated clip of a candidate is widely shared and believed
options.text: A fabricated clip of a candidate is widely shared and believed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Here a fake is made and believed. The liar's dividend is the dismissal of real evidence as fake, as when a person caught on a genuine recording says it was made by AI.

options.html: An employee sends money after a video call with faked colleagues
options.text: An employee sends money after a video call with faked colleagues
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is fraud by impersonation, in which a fake is believed. The liar's dividend is the dismissal of real evidence as fake.

options.html: A website strips the provenance record from an uploaded photograph
options.text: A website strips the provenance record from an uploaded photograph
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is a limit of provenance tools. The liar's dividend is the dismissal of real evidence as fake, as when a person caught on a genuine recording says it was made by AI.

options.html: A person caught on a genuine recording says it was made by AI
options.text: A person caught on a genuine recording says it was made by AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The liar's dividend is the benefit gained by calling real evidence fake when the public knows convincing fakes exist. No fake has to be made or believed.

forms.stemHtml: According to the authors who coined the term, what makes the liar's dividend grow?

options.html: Greater public awareness that convincing fakes exist
options.text: Greater public awareness that convincing fakes exist
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Chesney and Citron wrote that the dividend flows in proportion to success in educating the public about the dangers of deepfakes.

options.html: A rise in the number of fakes that people have believed
options.text: A rise in the number of fakes that people have believed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The dividend doesn't depend on any fake being believed. It grows with public awareness that convincing fakes exist.

options.html: Wider adoption of provenance records by news publishers
options.text: Wider adoption of provenance records by news publishers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Provenance records give people a way to check evidence. The dividend grows with public awareness that convincing fakes exist.

options.html: Stricter legal penalties for people who create deepfakes
options.text: Stricter legal penalties for people who create deepfakes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Penalties aren't part of the mechanism. The dividend grows with public awareness that convincing fakes exist.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about provenance records and labels for AI-generated content are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A label or record can be removed from a file
options.text: A label or record can be removed from a file
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Metadata can be lost when a file is screenshotted, re-saved, or uploaded to a service that strips it, and watermarks can be weakened by editing.

options.html: A file with no label can be assumed to be genuine
options.text: A file with no label can be assumed to be genuine
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Content made with a tool that doesn't mark its output, or with the mark removed, carries no label. The absence of a label tells you nothing.

options.html: An intact record from camera to publication is a reason to trust a file
options.text: An intact record from camera to publication is a reason to trust a file
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A provenance record is strongest as positive evidence of where content came from.

options.html: Adoption by devices, software, and sites is incomplete
options.text: Adoption by devices, software, and sites is incomplete
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A record helps only if every step in a file's history supports the standard, and many devices and services don't.

title: Synthetic media, misinformation, and trust
